questions.q: Explain sexual reproduction in animals, including fertilisation and its types.
answer: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of male and female gametes.

answer.text: The male gamete is the sperm, produced in the testes, and the female gamete is the egg, or ovum, produced in the ovary. Fertilisation is the fusion of a sperm and an egg to form a single cell called the zygote, which is the beginning of a new individual.

In internal fertilisation, which occurs in humans, cows and birds, the fusion takes place inside the female body. In external fertilisation, seen in fish and frogs, it takes place outside the body, in water.
The zygote divides repeatedly to form an embryo and then a foetus, which develops into a new individual.

questions.q: Distinguish between viviparous and oviparous animals, and describe methods of asexual reproduction.

answer.text: Viviparous animals, such as humans and cows, give birth to live young ones, while oviparous animals, such as birds, frogs and insects, lay eggs from which the young later hatch. In some animals the young undergo metamorphosis, a drastic change of form, as a tadpole becomes a frog or a caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

In asexual reproduction a single parent produces offspring identical to itself. In budding, a bud grows out and separates, as in Hydra. In binary fission, the parent simply splits into two, as in Amoeba. Scientists can also produce an identical copy of an organism by cloning; the first cloned mammal was Dolly the sheep in 1996.
